newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH GDP GROWTH EASES BEYOND ANALYST PREDICTIONS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH GDP GROWTH EASES BEYOND ANALYST PREDICTIONS.

text.p: The growth of the Czech economy, as expected, continued to slow in the third quarter but at a quicker pace than anticipated by analysts.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) said on Thursday that third quarter GDP grew by 3.6 percent, year-on-year, putting GDP 4.0 percent higher for the first three quarters of 1996 than for the same period last year.
A Reuter survey of economists on Wednesday had predicted growth for the first three quarters of 1996 of about 4.2 percent.
"The most dynamic growth influence, as it was in the first half, was the development of trade," the CSU said in a statement.

In the third quarter, the statement said imports were 222.9 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of some 21.8 percent. Imports for the first three quarters totalled 618.0 billion crowns, an increase of 14.7 percent over the previous year.

Meanwhile, the statement said exports for the third quarter grew by 6.1 percent, year-on-year, to 183.7 billion crowns, putting the three quarter combined total at 529.9 billion crowns, or 5.1 percent.

"In the area of foreign trade, dynamic grwoth in the importing of goods and services was seen, with the yearly growth accelerating from 9.4 percent in the first quarter to 21.8 percent in the third quarter," the statement said.

"The quickening was influenced by the developement of import prices, which grew year-on-year by only 0.3 percent. Domestic production is therefore seeing competitive pressure from imports and is hurt by lower prices on the domestic market," it added.
The statement added that the greatest decline in growth was in the agricultural sector, due in part to climatic problems.
"The share of private sector creation of GDP was for the last quarter 77.3 percent, which means a year-on-year grwoth of about 7.9 percentage points," the statement said.
